affordance_manifest.success: `<text>` present (non-empty after trim) → appends item, prints `Added: "N) <text>"` to stdout, exit 0
affordance_manifest.error: missing/blank `<text>` → `Error: missing todo text` to stderr, exit 1 (`E_MISSING_TEXT`); corrupted store → corrupted-store message to stderr, exit 1, no write
affordance_manifest.empty: first `add` on a missing/empty store creates the store with exactly one item

tasks.title: Implement `todo add <text>` command
acceptance_criteria: `node bin/todo.js add "buy milk"` on an empty/missing store exits 0, prints
A second `add` appends (does not overwrite) — running `add` twice results in 2 items in
`node bin/todo.js add` (no text) exits 1, prints an `E_MISSING_TEXT` message to stderr, and
`node bin/todo.js add "   "` (whitespace-only) is treated the same as missing text
Text is stored trimmed (leading/trailing whitespace removed, interior whitespace preserved)

bugs.criterion: UC-AddTodo Error Case E_STORE_WRITE_FAILED / ux-behavior global convention 'never a bare stack trace'
bugs.repro: H=/tmp/x; mkdir -p $H; HOME=$H node bin/todo.js add seed; chmod 444 $H/.todo.json; chmod 555 $H; HOME=$H node bin/todo.js add second
bugs.expected: stderr `Error: could not save todo store: <reason>`, exit 1
bugs.actual: exit 1 with an uncaught StoreWriteError and a full Node stack trace (lib/todo-repository.js:65 -> bin/todo.js:27). cmdDone (bin/todo.js:73) and cmdRm (bin/todo.js:105) wrap save() correctly; cmdAdd does not.

bugs.criterion: UC-CompleteTodo Steps 2-4 and UC-RemoveTodo Steps 2-4 (index parsed before load; E_MISSING_INDEX = no store access)
bugs.repro: H=/tmp/y; mkdir -p $H; printf '{{bad' > $H/.todo.json; HOME=$H node bin/todo.js done; HOME=$H node bin/todo.js done abc; HOME=$H node bin/todo.js rm; HOME=$H node bin/todo.js rm abc
bugs.expected: `Error: missing index` for the bare form and `Error: "abc" is not a valid index` for the bad-index form - the store is never read
bugs.actual: all four print `Error: todo store is corrupted (...)`; the store is read on a path the spec says must not touch it and the user is told the wrong thing is wrong
